project_title_working: Dynamic single-cell niche remodeling and biophysical steric exclusion govern clinical trial attrition across human organs

core_paradox_anchor.paradox_statement: Human genetic target support and static healthy single-cell specificity fail to prevent >85% of Phase II-III clinical trial failures across organs because administrative registry stoppages obscure biological efficacy futility while disease progression induces single-cell target lineage drift and fibrotic/peritumoral macromolecular steric exclusion.

data_micro_probe.probe_dataset_or_cohort: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 (41,396 deduplicated Phase II-IV systemic/organ trials; 11,637 Deconfounded Scientific Cohort) + Open Targets v24.09 + 6-axis primary human single-cell & 10x Visium cohorts (237 clinical specimens)
data_micro_probe.signal_summary: Empirical signal probe verified all primary directions prior to full modeling: clause-aware stoppage deconvolution strips 51.4% operational halts (n=240 adjudication kappa=0.9413), exposing 1.57-fold IgG mAb efficacy futility excess (P=2.26e-4); healthy tau_0 performs near chance (AUROC=0.5387), whereas Dynamic Niche Accessibility reaches AUROC=0.6710 (DeLong P=1.11e-21, LODO zero-shot AUROC=0.6306) and combines additively with Open Targets human genetics (AUROC=0.7023).
